column2: A place's GDP is the sum of the value added by its companies. A company also buys from suppliers and pays wages that are spent in other businesses: that is the multiplier effect.

Value added = sales − inputs over the last 12 months. «With suppliers and wages» adds half of the inputs bought in the region and 35 % of the wages. Every year, the change in that contribution enters the province's GDP (70 %: the competition would have done the rest) and moves its GDP per person, which in turn moves the province's wages; if the company goes bankrupt or closes, it is subtracted.
Companies sell to each other. That is why a crisis in one sector travels to its suppliers, and the bankruptcy of a large company leaves unpaid debts at the banks and unemployment in its city.

Your inputs follow the world price of their raw materials. If one of your companies produces the input of another of yours in the same country, that input is 10 % cheaper (vertical integration). If you go bankrupt, the province loses jobs and demand for 12 months and the country's banks lose 60 % of your debt.
Sectors don't move alike: with high rates, construction and technology suffer; in a recession, luxury; expensive oil helps oil companies and hurts transport.

Every month each sector of each country moves toward a target: 50 + growth, recession, rates, war, commodities, banks, bankruptcies and the health of its customers. It moves by up to ±12 % the demand of your companies, the profits of the country's listed companies and the health of its banks.
A company is worth what someone pays for it: a competitor pays more because it gains customers (synergies); a fund pays for the cash flows; an individual usually offers less.

Three buyers bid according to the company's health (margin, reputation, growth and debt). Accepting is safe; asking for +10 or +20 % has a visible probability. If they refuse, they lower their offer by 3 %; after the second refusal they walk away. When you sell it, its contribution to GDP stays in the province.

Your companies move the economy and the economy moves your companies.
  • 🌐 Contribution: in each company's sheet you see its value added (sales − inputs), the effect on suppliers and wages (multiplier), the jobs, the taxes and what share of the province's and the country's GDP it represents. Every year that contribution enters the province's GDP.
  • 🔗 Chain: your inputs follow the world price; if one of your companies produces the input of another of yours, it is 10 % cheaper. A bankruptcy leaves unemployment in the province and losses at the banks.
  • 🏭 Sectors: in Country → Economy each sector has its health (50 = normal) with its causes; it moves the demand of your companies and the Stock Market.
  • 🤝 Sell: in your company's sheet, «Sell» opens the negotiation with three buyers.
  • 🛒 Other countries: in Companies for sale choose the country; you pay 3 % in fees.
  • 🏢 Map: the 🏢 mode paints each province's economic activity and marks your companies (the frame color is their group).
